attribution.note: Marcus cites Fortune but states the claim in his own voice as one of his listed grievances, and the passage's conclusion adopts it. He endorses it.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the statement and keeps the Fortune qualifier as a condition. It is a retrospective observation about performance through the post date.

contract.note: Reading 'efforts' as the 20% compute pledge for superalignment follows from the Fortune report the speaker cited, so this is an ordinary reading. The pledge runs four years with no interim schedule, so the result depends on reading 'never delivered' as either 'not yet allocated' or 'broken'.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own announcement sets the terms: 20% of compute secured to date, over four years, with many teams expected to contribute. It sets no interim schedule and is not evidence of delivery.

Anonymous sources told Fortune the Superalignment team got far less than 20% and had flex requests rejected. This covers one team, not all qualifying work. The same report says the calculation and schedule were never defined, so it does not meet the support condition.

WIRED reports the team was disbanded and its work absorbed into other groups, and Leike says his team struggled for compute. Neither shows the commitment was conclusively abandoned or gives a company-wide percentage.

reviews.rationale: Credible anonymous reporting says the Superalignment team got far less than 20%. But the pledge ran four years, had no interim schedule, and expected many teams to contribute. No allocation records show the company-wide share, and the team's dissolution does not prove abandonment. The packet meets neither the support nor the contradiction condition.
